findings.title: LLM as a Risk Manager: LLM Semantic Filtering for Lead-Lag Trading in Prediction Markets
findings.reasoning: Zero hits anywhere in wiki/ or dream_cycle/ for the arXiv ID, 'lead-lag', 'Granger causality', or 'risk manager' in a prediction-markets context. Two-stage screener (Granger causality on Kalshi Economics probability paths, then LLM semantic-plausibility filtering) is mechanistically distinct from every existing PM strategy on the page (cross-platform arbitrage, single-contract Wang-transform mispricing, semantic pair-equivalence matching across platforms). Reported results: 18 rolling evals, win rate 51.4%->54.5%, avg losing trade $649->$347, total PnL >2x at 7-day horizon, framed explicitly as downside-risk reduction rather than raw alpha. Staged as a wiki research note (risk_level low) rather than a hypothesis spec, since replicating it needs historical Kalshi Economics probability-path time series broader than what the H185 pipeline currently pulls, plus the full PDF for LLM/threshold/contract-universe details not recoverable from the abstract.

findings.title: Factor-Augmented Machine Learning Panel Regressions
findings.reasoning: Confirmed genuinely new via grep (zero hits anywhere). Authors Babii/Barbaglia/Ghysels/Striaukas develop asymptotic theory for a factor-augmented sparse-group LASSO estimator combining MIDAS aggregation with latent factors for high-dimensional panels with cross-sectionally dependent errors. This is pure econometric estimator theory (econ.EM/math.ST/stat.ME/stat.ML cross-listed) -- no empirical trading application, no backtested strategy, no dataset applied to equities/ETFs. Judged not directly actionable for the hypothesis pipeline without a concrete signal-construction proposal layered on top, which the paper itself doesn't provide. Noted here rather than staged per the 'directly actionable, not just interesting' bar in tonight's task instructions.
